newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher in full volume.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher in full volume.

text.p: French shares finished at a high for the year, following a run up on bonds and the Dow, traders said.

The markets' welcome to Bill Clinton's presidential re-election sparked a buying spree in Paris, with a massive 7.3 billion francs of turnover. "It's an exceptional volume," said one trader. "This is not a rise in a vacuum."
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 26.05 points or 1.19 percent at 2,213.37, after hitting a session high of 2,218.57. The CAC-40 futures contract was up 25 at 2,218 from Tuesday's close.
* On the charts, the next commonly-cited target is 2,260 on the CAC index, following the breakthrough at 2,200.

* "If interest rates continue to come down, there is no reason why the market should not continue to rise, but some people are cautious as the market is from now on at the level many forecast we would be at the end of the year," one trader said.
* However, another trader said after two days of strong gains, the market should consolidate, but added that the heavy volumes suggested the rise could continue.
* Carrefour rises 2.37 percent to 3,021 francs, helped by its October sales figures, which showed a 12.3 percent increase to 14.54 billion francs
* Michelin ends up 3.38 percent at 260 francs, with buying sparked by nine-month sales figures
* SBC-Warburg put out a note which said it was "neutral" on Roussel Uclaf and "buy" Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
* CGIP puts on 3.36 percent to 1,230. The holding company and its parent sold a combined 2.4 million shares in Cap Gemini.
* Moulinex posts highest gain, up 5.11 percent to 105 francs. Traders said DB Bourse and SGE Delahaye were buyers.

* Pernod-Ricard up 2.83 percent at 294.5 francs. Managing director Thierry Jacquillat said that the French spirits market could fall by two to three percent in 1997 as a result of a rise in the spirits tax.
* LVMH and Dior rise respectively 3.96 percent to 1,260 and 2.46 percent to 709. Goldman Sachs rated them as outperform.
* Zodiac gains 3.54 percent to 1,522, helped by order for 120 Airbus jets by USAir airline.
